_comment: Adapter-specific declarations for the fleet tooling (Entwicklung/scripts). They live HERE so that a change in this adapter never touches the locked tooling. Readers: sync-iopackage-from-i18n.py (manifestI18n, release gate B03) and submit-stable.py (forumThread). Keys starting with an underscore are comments.

manifestI18n._comment: instanceObjects id -> key in admin/i18n/<lang>.json. Every manifest object needs a `name` entry (an object without one is a structural error, and so is an entry whose object no longer exists); `desc` only where the name does not already say it - an empty desc beats an invented sentence.
manifestI18n._note: The container object (info) has nothing to explain, hence no desc.

_forkOf: The repository descends from Christopher Holomek's GitHub project (his commits from 2020 are in the history); README `## Credits` names him (CLAUDE_README.md point 11).
_listenPorts: Fleet standard since 2026-09-15 (Entwicklung/CLAUDE_PATTERNS.md, section listen-port declaration; enforced by the check listen-port-declaration): the primary port lives in native.port as a number, the listen address in native.bind — the pair the admin's port-conflict check reads. httpsPort is the optional second listener of this bridge. `ssdp` is a label, not a native key: the SSDP port 1900 (SSDP_PORT in src/discovery/ssdp-server.ts) is shared with every other UPnP adapter on the host by design and is therefore never native.port. httpsPort stays a text field with its own validator: ConfigPort reads native.port only, so a secondary listener cannot take part in the admin's conflict detection anyway.

serverTest._why: The build comes up on the real host and serves: the HTTP and HTTPS listeners and SSDP are up, which is when the adapter sets info.connection to true.
serverTest.noCommands: Its only writable states are the bridge's own settings, disableAuth and startPairing: switching either on the live host opens access for every client on the network. Lights are switched by Hue clients over HTTP, never through a state of this adapter.

suites._comment: What the fleet suites in test/fleet-suites.js need to know (B02 audit_inventory_runs_fleet_suites).

connectionTest.none: The settings page has no connection test (no sendTo field) and no device manager card has a test action: the adapter connects to nothing, Hue clients connect to it.

groupSwitches.none: The adapter has no switch that turns a group of datapoints on or off.

rejectLogin.none: The adapter logs in nowhere: it holds no account and no device login, its only secret is the key of its own self-signed TLS certificate, kept encrypted in the instance data folder, not in native.

dropDevice.none: No counterpart (krobi 2026-10-02 22:05: "das gerät kann nie weg sein"): a light is the adapter's own Hue view of ioBroker datapoints, not a device that can go away. lights.<n>.reachable says whether the bridge can drive the light from its bound datapoints (design decision 26); a deleted bound datapoint turns it false in the unit tests of main.ts and device-binding-service.ts.

noDeviceSums: No counterpart (krobi 2026-10-02 22:05: "das gerät kann nie weg sein"): a light is a Hue view of ioBroker datapoints, not a device that is online or offline. lights.<n>.reachable only says whether its bound datapoints exist, so a count of lights online would count the configuration, not devices.

deviceIds.assigned: The device manager gives every light a permanent number once (lights.<n>, src/lib/light-store.ts, design decision 25): it is the light's Hue id and uniqueid for every paired client and is never handed out again. A light has no unit id of its own, and its name is free and may repeat.

fixtureLimits.none: No own datapoint takes over the limits of a device: the value ranges live on the bound foreign datapoints, which the adapter reads and never copies.
